newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rains dampen down cocoa, grain prices.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rains dampen down cocoa, grain prices.

text.p: World cocoa and grain prices eased on Tuesday on reports of welcome rains in major growing areas of those weather sensitive crops.
Elsewhere the base metals complex remained volatile although, apart from lead and aluminium, overall movements were small.

On the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) cocoa market the September futures contract dropped 19 sterling a tonne to 994 sterling as speculators on the New York market sold out their holdings.

Strengthening rains in the world's number one producer Ivory Coast at the end of July should prove beneficial to the country's main crop and crop analysts said pod development was unaffected by low rainfall earlier in July as soil moisture had been kept up by cool temperatures, blanket cloud and torrential June rains.
In Chicago, corn and soyabean prices dropped on forecasts of wetter weather over the American Midwest growing areas.
Losses in corn were tempered slightly by a forecast by Sparks Companies, a private Memphis based firm, putting the U.S. crop at 9.47 million bushels, below the USDAs most recent forecast.
By midday September corn futures were trading around $2.59 a bushel, down five cents, while September soyabeans were down 4 cents at $6.73.
Investment funds took profits in aluminium and dumped recent positions they had built up in lead.

Traders said that aluminium had been due a correction after a strong rise recently to 22 month highs, and later in the day news that Canadian producer Alcan is to restart idled potlines at its Kitimat, British Columbia, smelter weighed on the market.
Three months delivery aluminium on the London Metal Exchange (LME) ended the day at $1,721 a tonne, down $23 from Monday.
A recent speculative bubble in lead collapsed today with traders unable to cite any particular fundamental reason for the original rise or the fall, apart from chart patterns and investor interest.
Lead closed $32 a tonne lower on the LME at $605.
